question_html: Which of the following books is considered a principal book of accounts rather than a subsidiary book?
answer_html: Answer: (B) The ledger and cash book are principal books, while purchases, sales, and returns books are subsidiary books[cite: 10].
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: What is another name for books of original entry or prime entry?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Books of original or prime entry are also called subsidiary books[cite: 10].
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: Which of the following transactions is recorded in the Purchases Book?

options.C: Credit purchases of goods dealt in by the firm

answer_html: Answer: (C) Purchases Book records credit purchases of goods dealt in or materials required in the business[cite: 10].
topic_text: Purchases Book and Recording of Credit Purchases

question_html: Where are credit sales of items other than goods dealt in by the firm recorded?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Credit sales of items other than goods dealt in are journalised in the Journal Proper.
topic_text: Sales Book and Recording of Credit Sales

question_html: What type of balance does a Returns Outward (Purchase Returns) Account typically show?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Purchase returns account shows a credit balance because it reduces purchases / assets go out.
topic_text: Sales Returns (Returns Inward) and Purchase Returns (Returns Outward) Books

question_html: Which advantage of subsidiary books helps in locating errors easily when a trial balance does not agree? (Scenario 6)
answer_html: Answer: (C) Existence of separate books facilitates the checking and location of errors when a trial balance fails to agree.
topic_text: Advantages of Subsidiary Books

question_html: Which of the following transactions should be recorded in the Journal Proper? (Scenario 7)

options.A: Credit purchase of goods for resale
options.B: Opening entries at the start of a new accounting year
options.D: Receipt of cash from a trade receivable

answer_html: Answer: (B) Opening entries are recorded in the Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: When calculating the net amount of a credit purchase to be entered in the Purchases Book, trade discount is: (Scenario 8)

options.D: Credited to discount received account separately

answer_html: Answer: (B) Trade discount is deducted from the gross amount, and the net amount is entered in the amount column.
topic_text: Purchases Book and Recording of Credit Purchases

question_html: When goods are returned by a customer, what document is issued to them? (Scenario 9)
answer_html: Answer: (B) A credit note is issued to the customers concerned showing the amount to be credited to their account.
topic_text: Sales Returns (Returns Inward) and Purchase Returns (Returns Outward) Books

question_html: The dishonour of a bill received from a customer is recorded in which book? (Scenario 10)
answer_html: Answer: (C) Entries on dishonour of bills require journalising in the Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: What is the primary function of the Sales Returns (Returns Inward) Book? (Scenario 11)

options.A: To record goods returned to suppliers
options.B: To record goods returned by customers
options.D: To record bad debts written off

answer_html: Answer: (B) Returns inward book records the return of goods made by the customers sold to them earlier.
topic_text: Sales Returns (Returns Inward) and Purchase Returns (Returns Outward) Books

question_html: When a firm returns goods to a supplier, what document does the returning firm issue to indicate the debiting of the supplier's account? (Scenario 12)
answer_html: Answer: (B) The firm returning the goods will issue a debit note to the supplier, indicating the amount for which the supplier account is being debited.
topic_text: Sales Returns (Returns Inward) and Purchase Returns (Returns Outward) Books

question_html: What is posted to the credit of the Sales Account at the end of a period? (Scenario 13)

options.B: Total of the Sales Book (credit sales)

answer_html: Answer: (B) The total of the Sales Book shows the credit sales made during the period, which is credited to the Sales Account.
topic_text: Sales Book and Recording of Credit Sales

question_html: Which of the following is an advantage of using subsidiary books? (Scenario 14)

options.B: Division of work among different clerks leading to specialization
options.C: Guarantee of zero errors in books

answer_html: Answer: (B) Division of work and specialization/efficiency are key advantages of subsidiary books.
topic_text: Advantages of Subsidiary Books

question_html: Where are cash receipts and cash payments recorded? (Scenario 15)
answer_html: Answer: (B) Cash Book is used to record receipts and payments of cash, including bank transactions.
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: If a second-hand motor car is purchased on credit from B Brothers for ₹10,000, how should it be recorded? (Scenario 16)
answer_html: Answer: (C) Credit purchase of items other than goods dealt in (such as second-hand motor car / fixed assets) is recorded in the Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: An allowance of ₹50 offered for early payment of cash of ₹1,050 received from a debtor is recorded in which book of original entry? (Scenario 17)
answer_html: Answer: (B) Cash book with discount column is used to record cash receipts/payments along with cash/trade/settlement discounts allowed or received.
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: Where is a bills receivable of ₹1,000 received from a debtor in full settlement for a claim of ₹1,100, which is subsequently dishonoured, recorded? (Scenario 18)
answer_html: Answer: (C) Dishonour of bills and related adjustments are recorded in the Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: What is the correct treatment for the weekly or monthly total of the Purchases Book when posting to the ledger? (Scenario 19)

options.A: Posted to the debit of the Purchases Account
options.B: Posted to the credit of the Purchases Account
options.C: Posted to the debit of the Sales Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) The total of the amounts column shows total purchases made; the amount is debited to the Purchase Account.
topic_text: Purchases Book and Recording of Credit Purchases

question_html: How are individual supplier accounts credited when recording entries from the Purchases Book? (Scenario 20)

options.A: By individual net amounts shown for each supplier in the purchases book
options.B: By gross amounts before trade discount
options.C: By total purchases of the year combined
options.D: Suppliers are debited instead of credited

answer_html: Answer: (A) Suppliers' accounts are credited for the respective net amounts shown in the purchase book.
topic_text: Purchases Book and Recording of Credit Purchases

question_html: What is the accounting implication if freight charged by a supplier is entered in the Purchases Book along with goods? (Scenario 21)

options.A: Freight is posted to a separate Freight Account and supplier's total includes freight.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Freight charged is segregated into a Freight Account (debited) while the supplier's account is credited with the total inclusive amount.
topic_text: Purchases Book and Recording of Credit Purchases

question_html: Why are cash purchases excluded from the Purchases Book? (Scenario 22)

options.A: Because cash purchases are entered directly in the Cash Book.
options.B: Because cash purchases violate accounting standards.
options.C: Because cash purchases must be journalised in Journal Proper.
options.D: Because cash purchases are treated as credit sales.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Cash purchases are not entered in the purchases book since these are entered in the cash book.
topic_text: Purchases Book and Recording of Credit Purchases

question_html: How is the total of the Sales Returns Book posted into the ledger? (Scenario 23)

options.A: Debited to Sales Returns (Returns Inward) Account and individual customers are credited.
options.B: Credited to Sales Returns Account and customers are debited.
options.C: Credited to Sales Account directly without returns account.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Total sales returns is debited to Returns Inward Account and customers who returned goods are credited.
topic_text: Sales Returns (Returns Inward) and Purchase Returns (Returns Outward) Books

question_html:
What does the Practical System of Book-keeping (English System) entail regarding subsidiary books? (Scenario 24)

transactions of a class are first recorded in a specialized book and ledger accounts are prepared on that basis without routine journal entries for each transaction.

options.A: Transactions of a class are first recorded in a specialized book, and ledger accounts are prepared on that basis without routine journal entries for each transaction.
options.B: Every single transaction must pass through the general journal first.
options.C: Ledgers are maintained before any books of original entry.
options.D: Subsidiary books replace trial balance entirely.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Transactions of a class are first recorded in a specified book specially meant for it, on the basis of which ledger accounts are then prepared.
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: Which of the following entries requires a journal entry in the Journal Proper rather than a subsidiary book? (Scenario 25)

options.A: Credit sale of goods to a regular customer
options.B: Transfer of net profit to capital account at year end
options.C: Cash received from sale of goods

answer_html: Answer: (B) Transfer entries like transferring net profit to capital account require journalising in Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: What is the nature and posting rule for the Bills Receivable Book? (Scenario 26)

options.A: It records promissory notes received; individual parties are credited and bills receivable total is debited.
options.B: It records bills issued; parties are debited.
options.C: It is a principal ledger account.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Bills receivable book records receipts of promissory notes from parties, who are credited while bills receivable account is debited.
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: Why are adjusting entries at the end of the year (such as for outstanding expenses or depreciation) recorded in the Journal Proper? (Scenario 27)

options.A: Because no specialized subsidiary book like purchases or sales book is meant for year-end adjustments.
options.B: Because adjusting entries involve cash receipts.
options.C: Because they must bypass the ledger.
options.D: Because they are prohibited by ICAI standards.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Adjusting entries for outstanding expenses, prepaid expenses, and depreciation are processed via journal entries in Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: If a firm purchases goods for cash, where is it entered? (Scenario 28)
answer_html: Answer: (B) Cash purchases are entered in the cash book, not in the purchases book.
topic_text: Purchases Book and Recording of Credit Purchases

question_html: What is the distinction between Subsidiary Books and Principal Books? (Scenario 29)

options.A: Subsidiary books are books of original entry where transactions are first recorded, whereas principal books (ledger and cash book) furnish information for trial balance and financial statements.
options.B: Principal books record individual invoices while subsidiary books prepare final balance sheets.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Subsidiary books record transactions first to enable further processing, while the ledger and cash book are principal books furnishing information for trial balance and financial statements.
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: How are customer accounts posted from the Sales Book? (Scenario 30)

options.A: Debited with the respective net amount of sales made to them

answer_html: Answer: (A) Names appearing in the sales book receive goods, so their accounts are debited with respective amounts.
topic_text: Sales Book and Recording of Credit Sales

question_html: What is the effect of recording transactions in subsidiary books on the double-entry accounting system? (Scenario 31)

options.A: There is no departure from the rules of the double-entry system.
options.B: It replaces double entry with single entry.
options.D: It eliminates the need for ledger posting.

answer_html: Answer: (A) In this practical system, there is no departure from the rules of the double entry system.
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: If an amount becomes irrecoverable because a customer becomes insolvent, where is this bad debt recorded? (Scenario 32)
answer_html: Answer: (B) If an amount becomes irrecoverable due to insolvency, it requires journalising in the Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: Which of the following books records promissory notes or hundies issued to other parties? (Scenario 33)
answer_html: Answer: (B) Bills Payable Book records the issue of promissory notes or hundies to other parties.
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: What is the posting procedure for the Returns Outward Book total? (Scenario 34)

options.A: Credited to Returns Outward (Purchase Returns) Account and suppliers whose names appear are debited.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The total of returns outward book is credited to Purchase Returns/Returns Outward Account and suppliers are debited.
topic_text: Sales Returns (Returns Inward) and Purchase Returns (Returns Outward) Books

question_html: Why are subsidiary books also referred to as books of original entry? (Scenario 35)

options.A: Because transactions are recorded in them for the very first time from source documents before ledger posting.
options.B: Because they replace final balance sheets.
options.C: Because they are maintained only by head offices.
options.D: Because they contain opening entries exclusively.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Books in which transactions are first recorded to enable further processing are called subsidiary books or books of original entry.
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: What is the correct treatment when goods purchased for cash are returned to the supplier? (Scenario 36)

options.B: Recorded in Cash Book (as cash receipt)

answer_html: Answer: (B) Return of goods previously purchased for cash involves cash refund, which is handled through the Cash Book.
topic_text: Sales Returns (Returns Inward) and Purchase Returns (Returns Outward) Books

question_html: Which of the following is NOT a subsidiary book commonly used in business? (Scenario 37)
answer_html: Answer: (B) General Ledger is a principal book, not a subsidiary book[cite: 10].
topic_text: Introduction to Subsidiary Books and Practical System of Book-keeping

question_html: How are closing entries processed at the end of the accounting year? (Scenario 38)

options.A: Through journal entries in the Journal Proper transferring nominal accounts to P&L

answer_html: Answer: (A) Closing entries transferring nominal accounts to profit and loss account are done through journal entries in Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: What is the significance of the particulars column in a Purchases Book? (Scenario 39)

options.A: It records the name of the supplier, name of articles purchased, and quantities.
options.B: It records cash discount percentages only.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The particulars column is meant to record the name of the supplier and name of the articles purchased and respective quantities.
topic_text: Purchases Book and Recording of Credit Purchases

question_html: If a firm does not maintain separate bills receivable and bills payable books, where are promissory notes received or issued recorded? (Scenario 40)
answer_html: Answer: (A) Receipt or issue of promissory notes, if separate bill books have not been maintained, requires journalising in Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: What is the reporting treatment of the total of the Sales Book in the ledger? (Scenario 41)
answer_html: Answer: (A) The total of the sales book shows credit sales made; the amount is credited to the Sales Account.
topic_text: Sales Book and Recording of Credit Sales

question_html: How does the use of subsidiary books save time in an accounting department? (Scenario 42)

options.A: Various accounting processes and recordings can be undertaken simultaneously by multiple clerks because of multiple books.
options.B: It eliminates the need for bookkeeping altogether.
options.D: It stops transactions from happening on weekends.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Various accounting processes can be undertaken simultaneously because of the use of a number of books, leading to quick completion.
topic_text: Advantages of Subsidiary Books

question_html: Which book is used to record the return of goods sold to customers earlier? (Scenario 43)
answer_html: Answer: (B) Sale returns book records the returns of goods made by the customers sold to them earlier.
topic_text: Sales Returns (Returns Inward) and Purchase Returns (Returns Outward) Books

question_html: What is the correct ledger posting for individual customer accounts from the Sales Returns Book? (Scenario 44)

options.A: Credited with the respective amount of returned goods

answer_html: Answer: (A) The customers who have returned the goods are credited with the respective amounts.
topic_text: Sales Returns (Returns Inward) and Purchase Returns (Returns Outward) Books

question_html: Where are rectifying entries for accounting errors recorded? (Scenario 45)
answer_html: Answer: (B) Rectification entries for committed errors are executed through the Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: What is the primary advantage of keeping a separate register for each class of transactions (subsidiary books)? (Scenario 46)

options.A: Information relating to each class of transaction is available conveniently at one place.
options.C: It removes the need for a trial balance.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Availability of information relating to each class of transaction at one place is a major advantage.
topic_text: Advantages of Subsidiary Books

question_html: If a firm suffers a loss of property by fire, how is this event recorded? (Scenario 47)
answer_html: Answer: (A) Effects of accidents such as loss of property by fire require journalising in the Journal Proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions

question_html: What type of transactions are recorded in the Sales Book? (Scenario 48)

options.A: Credit sales of goods dealt in by the firm
options.C: Sales of fixed assets on credit

answer_html: Answer: (A) Sales Book is a register specially kept to record credit sales of goods dealt in by the firm.
topic_text: Sales Book and Recording of Credit Sales

question_html: Why are credit purchases of office furniture or typewriters not entered in the Purchases Book? (Scenario 49)

options.A: Because furniture and typewriters are not goods dealt in or materials required for production; they are fixed assets journalised separately.
options.B: Because fixed assets cannot be bought on credit.
options.C: Because they must be recorded in the sales book.
options.D: Because they are exempt from accounting.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Credit purchases of items other than goods or materials (such as office furniture) are journalised in Journal Proper - not entered in the Purchases Book.
topic_text: Purchases Book and Recording of Credit Purchases

question_html: What is the fundamental role of the Journal Proper when subsidiary books are operational in an entity? (Scenario 50)

options.A: To record all transactions and events that cannot be accommodated in any of the specialized subsidiary books.
options.B: To replace the cash book entirely.
options.C: To record daily cash sales exclusively.

answer_html: Answer: (A) If there is no special book meant to record a transaction, it is recorded in the journal proper.
topic_text: Journal Proper and Classification of Unallocated Transactions
